source: Dallas City Code ch. 51P, Article 787 (City Attorney's codified article, April 2026)

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-787.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 787 was established by Ordinance No. 27212, passed by the Dallas City Council on June 11, 2008. (Ord. 27212)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-787.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 787 is established on property located on the south side of Northwest Highway, east of Lemmon Avenue. The size of PD 787 is approximately 13.19 acres. (Ord. 27212)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-787.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to the article.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A. In this district:

(1) BLADE SIGN means a sign projecting perpendicularly from a main building facade that is visible from both sides.

(2) STOOP means a small porch leading to the entrance of a residence.

(3) OPEN SPACE means an area used for recreational and gathering purposes that contains only landscaping, hardscaping, and structures with omitted walls.

(c) This district is considered to be a residential zoning district. (Ord. 27212)

sections.title: Creation Of Subareas
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-787.104. CREATION OF SUBAREAS.

This district is divided into six subareas: Subareas 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 as shown on the conceptual plan. (Ord. 27212)

sections.title: Exhibit
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-787.105. EXHIBIT.

The following exhibit is incorporated into this article: Exhibit 787A: conceptual plan. (Ord. 27212)

sections.title: Conceptual Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-787.106. CONCEPTUAL PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the conceptual plan (Exhibit 787A). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the conceptual plan, the text of this article controls. (Ord. 27212)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-787.107. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(a) Except as provided in this section, a development plan for each subarea must be approved by the city plan commission before the issuance of any building permit to authorize work in that subarea. If there is a conflict between the conceptual plan and an approved development plan, the approved development plan controls. If there is a conflict between the text of this article and an approved development plan, the text of this article controls.

(b) In Subareas 2 and 3, a final plat may serve as the development plan for a single family development. (Ord. Nos. 27212; 30583)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-787.108. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Subareas 1, 2, 3, 5, and 6. The following uses are the only main uses permitted:

-- Duplex. -- Handicapped group dwelling unit. [SUP required if spacing component of Section 51A-4.209(3.1) is not met.] -- Local utilities. -- Multifamily. -- Private recreation center, club, or area. [SUP] -- Private street or alley. -- Public park, playground, or golf course. -- Retirement housing. -- Single family.

(b) Subarea 4. The following main use is the only main use permitted:

-- Public park, playground, or golf course. (Ord. 27212)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-787.109. ACCESSORY USES.

(a) As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any subarea in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A-4.217.

(b) The following accessory uses are not permitted:

-- Accessory helistop.

-- Accessory medical/infectious waste incinerator. -- Accessory outside display or sale of merchandise. -- Accessory pathological waste incinerator. -- Amateur communication tower. -- Day home. -- General waste incinerator. -- Pedestrian skybridges. -- Private stable. (Ord. 27212)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-787.110. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Division 51A-4.400. If there is a conflict between this section and Division 51A-4.400, this section controls.)

(a) In general. Setbacks between subareas are not required.

(b) Front yard.

(1) Single family uses.

(A) Except as provided in this paragraph, minimum front yard is 10 feet.

(B) Along Northwest Highway, minimum front yard is 20 feet as shown on the conceptual plan.

(C) Balconies, bay windows, stoops, signs, and entryways may project up to five feet into the required front yard if the total combined area of these projections does not exceed 10 percent of the required front yard.

(2) Other uses. Minimum front yard is 20 feet.

(c) Side and rear yard.

(1) Except as provided in this subsection, for single family uses, no side or rear yard is required.

(2) Except as provided in this subsection, for all other uses, minimum side yard is as shown on the conceptual plan and minimum rear yard is 15 feet.

(3) For carports and single-story parking structures:

(A) Minimum side and rear yard of five feet must be provided along southern and eastern Property line;

(B) No side or rear yard must be provided along the western Property line.

(4) Balconies, bay windows, stoops, signs, and entryways may project up to four feet into the required side or rear yard if the total combined area of these projections does not exceed 10 percent of the required side or rear yard.

(d) Density.

(1) In Subareas 1, 2, 5, and 6, maximum total number of dwelling units is 487.

(2) In Subarea 3, maximum number of dwelling units is 32.

(e) Floor area. No maximum floor area, except that maximum floor area for all accessory uses combined is 10,000 square feet.

(f) Height.

(1) Residential proximity slope.

(A) In general. If any portion of a structure is over 26 feet in height, that portion may not be located above a 1-to-3 residential proximity slope. See Section 51A-4.412 for site of origination.

(B) Subareas 2 and 3. Subarea 2 and Subarea 3 do not apply when determining the site of origination for a residential proximately slope.

(2) Single-story parking structures. Single-story parking structures may not exceed 16 feet in height. See Section 51P-787.114(e) for facade requirements.

(3) Maximum structure height. Unless further restricted in Paragraph (1), maximum structure height is:

(A) Subarea 1: 36 feet in the area between 10 feet and 48 feet from the western property line; otherwise 60 feet.

(B) Subarea 2: 45 feet.

(C) Subarea 3: 35 feet.

(D) Subarea 4: 22 feet.

(E) Subarea 5: 70 feet.

(F) Subarea 6: 36 feet in the area between 10 feet and 48 feet from the western property line; otherwise, 80 feet.

(g) Lot coverage.

(1) Maximum lot coverage is 70 percent.

(2) For purposes of calculating lot coverage, the Property is considered one lot.

(3) Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking lots, carports, and underground parking structures are not.

(h) Lot size. No minimum lot size.

(i) Stories. Maximum number of stories above grade is:

(1) Subarea 1: four.

(2) Subarea 2: three.

(3) Subarea 3: two.

(4) Subarea 4: no maximum.

(5) Subarea 5: five.

(6) Subarea 6: six.

(j) Open space. A minimum of five percent of the Property must be open space. (Ord. Nos. 27212; 30584)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-787.111. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, consult the use regulations in Division 51A-4.200 for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(b) Multifamily uses.

(1) One off-street parking space is required for each 500 square feet of dwelling unit floor area.

(2) Not less than one off-street parking space or more than two off-street parking spaces are required for each dwelling unit.

(c) Compact parking. A maximum of 25 percent of the required off-street parking may be compact parking. (Ord. 27212)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-787.112. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 27212)

sections.title: Landscaping
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-787.113. LANDSCAPING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, landscaping, tree mitigation, and tree preservation must be provided in accordance with Article X.

(b) Screening. The screening requirements in Section 51A-4.602(b) do not apply along the southern boundary of the Property.

(c) Site trees. One site tree must be provided for every 6,000 square feet of lot area.

(d) Location. Required trees must be planted no closer than 2.5 feet from a curb or paved surface. Large trees must be planted no closer than 10 feet from a building wall and no closer than 20 feet from another large tree.

(e) Tree mitigation.

(1) To qualify for a reduction in the number of replacement trees, the building official must determine that the tree protection requirements in Article X have been met.

(2) The total caliper inches of replacement trees required may be reduced by a factor of 1.5 for every existing large tree with a caliper of 20 inches or greater that is preserved. For example, a tree with a caliper of 20 inches that is preserved reduces the tree replacement requirement by 30 caliper inches. The purpose of this provision is to encourage the preservation of existing trees. As used in this provision, “existing” means a tree that existed on June 11, 2008, the date of creation of this district.

(3) Yaupon holly, Ilex vomitoria, is not a protected tree, but relocation of yaupon hollies is encouraged.

(4) If the property owner submits an application for a building permit for a building within six months after the issuance of an approved tree removal application, tree mitigation must be completed before the final certificate of occupancy is issued on the Property, or within 36 months after the tree removal application is approved, whichever is sooner. Otherwise, tree mitigation must be completed as required by Section 51A-10.134(5).

(5) Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 27212)

sections.title: Parking Structure Facades
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-787.114. PARKING STRUCTURE FACADES.

(a) Except as provided in this section, parking structure facades must have a facade that is similar in materials, architecture, and appearance to the facade of the main structure or the adjacent structure.

(b) Breaks in a parking structure facade not exceeding 40 feet in width are permitted at entrances and exits.

(c) Openings in a parking structure facade may not exceed 50 percent of the total parking structure facade area.

(d) Openings in a parking structure facade that are visible from a public right-of-way, other than entrances and exits, may not exceed 45 percent of the total parking structure facade area.

(e) At least 70 percent of the facade of a single-story parking structure, exclusive of openings, must have materials similar to the main residential structure the parking serves. (Ord. 27212)

sections.title: Sidewalks
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-787.115. SIDEWALKS.

A minimum six-foot-wide sidewalk must be provided along Northwest Highway. (Ord. 27212)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-787.116. SIGNS.

(a) Except as provided in this section, signs must comply with the provisions for non- business zoning districts in Article VII.

(b) For multifamily uses, two additional blade premise signs are permitted. The effective area of the two additional blade premise signs may not exceed 68 square feet for each side. The two additional blade premise signs must be attached to a main structure and may not be internally lighted. (Ord. 27212)

SEC. 51P-787.116.1. SHARED ACCESS DEVELOPMENT

(a) A shared access development in Subareas 2 or 3 may not exceed a maximum of 33 lots and must have a minimum of one access point.

(b) An emergency-only access point connecting to a fire lane on an adjacent property within the district must be provided for a shared access development with one access point in Subareas 2 and 3. (Ord. 30583)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-787.117. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 27212)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-787.118. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the director of public works and transportation.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 27212)
